sentences.text: This is first bail application under Section 438 of Cr.P.C for grant of anticipatory bail in connection with crime No.261/2023 dated : not mentioned, registered at P.S. - Palsood District - Badwani for offences punishable under Sections 366 (A), 376, 376(2)(n), 506 of IPC and 3/4, 5L/6 of POCSO Act.
2. It is alleged that a report was lodged by mother of the prosecutrix that her 13 years old daughter was missing.

Thereafter, the prosecutrix was recovered and the aforesaid offence were registered.
3.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The prosecutrix is a major lady and she herself had gone alongwith the prosecutrix and made physical relationship.
4. Learned counsel for the prosecutrix has no objection to grant bail to the applicant.

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the respondent/state opposed the prayer.
However, fairly submits that as per the scholar register, the prosecutrix is about 19 years.
Thus, she was major at the time of incident.

6. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the statement of the prosecutrix and the age as per scholar register that she is major, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled for anticipatory bail.
Therefore, without commenting on merits of the case, the application is allowed.

7. It is further directed that in case if the applicant Ajay furnishes personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rs.Fifty Thousand only) with separate surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Investigating Officer
, then they shall be released by the Investigating Officer.

The applicant shall further abide by all the conditions as enumerated under section 437(3) Cr.P.C.
(VIJAY KUMAR SHUKLA) JUDGE Sourabh Ajay vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83583776/
